shortlist.excerpt: Our construction phase will create approximately 15,000 union construction jobs with average wages of approximately $55 per hour, representing a transformative economic impact through specific diversity commitments that directly benefit historically underserved and local communities. We have established aggressive workforce diversity targets for construction that reflect our understanding that meaningful economic development requires intentional investment in historically underrepresented communities: 40% minority workers (6,000 jobs), 10% women workers (1,500 jobs), and 10% veteran workers (1,500 jobs).

shortlist.excerpt: CONSTRUCTION 3 EvalLoc4.Bally’s.Communities This model has proven highly effective in achieving economic inclusion goals, with our Chicago construction collective surpassing our goals of 36% of construction spend with certified Minority-Owned Business Enterprises (MBE), 10% with certified Women- Owned Business Enterprises (WBE), 50% of project hours worked by City of Chicago residents and 15.5% participation from Socioeconomically Disadvantaged Areas (SEDA). Our approach to supplier diversity is driven by clear and measurable goals that align with New York State’s expectations to uplift underserved communities.
